transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Lauren (Elmstreet Head of Data), Aaron (Elmstreet SRE), Priya (Elmstreet Security), Tom (Elmstreet PM), Kelvin (Elmstreet Compliance)

Summary: Quick POC scoping focused on security/compliance needs for a 2-week pilot. Discussed success criteria (accuracy, latency, cost), workload sizing (QPS, token counts), benchmark plan, timelines, and detailed security controls (SOC 2, ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, VPC). Agreed next steps: Redwood to share security artifacts and pilot scope, schedule bench test, and provision trial environment.

Topics: POC success criteria; workload sizing; benchmark metrics; timeline for pilot; SOC2/ISO artifacts; SSO/SAML and IdP integration; RBAC and audit logging; KMS and key management; data residency and BAA considerations.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, um quick roll call, we have Elmstreet folks?
[00:09] Lauren Gomez: hey yeah Lauren here, Aaron, Priya, Tom, Kelvin are on too.
[00:14] Maya Chen: perfect, I'm Maya with Redwood, and Ravi is our solutions engineer, we wanted to run through the POC scope, specifically security requirements since you're in healthcare.
[00:26] Ravi Patel: hey all, hi, glad to meet you. we'll go over workload sizing and the benchmark plan as well.
[00:32] Tom Rivera: quick note, timeline is kind of tight for us — we want pilot results in about three weeks to present to procurement.
[00:40] Maya Chen: noted, we'll aim for a 2-week hands-on pilot + 1 week to analyze results.

[01:05] Lauren Gomez: high level our success criteria are: 1) accuracy of outputs compared to our baseline models, 2) P95 latency under 400ms for single-turn generation for typical prompt sizes, and 3) cost per 1k tokens under our threshold, also security must meet SOC2 plus internal policy.
[01:29] Priya Shah: on security, SOC 2 is table stakes, we also need ISO27001 artifacts, SSO via SAML with our Okta, RBAC for model access, detailed audit logs, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys. we may need a BAA if PHI is in scope.
[01:54] Maya Chen: absolutely, we regularly provide SOC2 and ISO artifacts. we have SAML SSO, and support for customer KMS/HSM. for PHI, we have private deployment options — Redwood Dedicated or Private VPC where data doesn't leave the customer's network.

[02:20] Aaron Li: can you explain the difference between Dedicated and Private? we want isolation but also don't want the full operational overhead.
[02:29] Ravi Patel: sure, Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity in our hosted environment with tenant isolation and no co-tenancy on the GPU pools. Private is a VPC or on-prem option where the control plane is separated and data lifecycles are customer-managed — slightly more setup but aligns with stricter compliance. Dedicated can be spun up faster for a pilot.
[02:50] Aaron Li: okay, for the pilot we'd prefer Dedicated if it gives us the KMS and audit control hooks.

[03:10] Kelvin Ortiz: do you have log retention policies and the ability to forward audit logs to our SIEM? we need tamper-evident logs and at least 1 year retention for audit.
[03:22] Maya Chen: yes, we can forward logs via syslog or a cloud logging endpoint. retention is configurable; for Dedicated pilots we can set retention rules and provide immutable audit trails and signed logs for tamper evidence.

[03:40] Lauren Gomez: workload sizing — we ingest ~500k API requests per month across a mix of short chat and doc summarization. for the POC we can narrow to a representative sample: ~5k requests/day, average prompt 120 tokens, average response 300 tokens.
[04:02] Ravi Patel: thanks, that maps to about 2M tokens/day in the pilot sample — for real-time we care about concurrency: what's your peak QPS?
[04:10] Aaron Li: peak about 18 QPS for the subset we'll test, sustained 5 QPS.
[04:16] Ravi Patel: good, for that we recommend starting with an 8-GPU pool (we'll suggest exact instance types) to meet P95 targets with batching and KV cache. we'll simulate the 18 QPS with our load harness.

[04:40] Tom Rivera: can we run benchmarks against our test dataset and measure both latency and output consistency? we have labeled references for summarization quality.
[04:49] Ravi Patel: yes, we'll run a deterministic benchmark against your dataset, produce token-latency distributions, throughput, and quality metrics (ROUGE/BLEU or custom eval). we'll also measure token cost and provide a per-1k token estimate.

[05:10] Priya Shah: for SAML, Okta is our IdP — what's the expected timeline for SSO integration? we need SAML metadata and an SP-initiated flow.
[05:19] Maya Chen: typically SSO can be configured within 3-5 business days for a pilot once we exchange metadata. for Dedicated pilots we can enable a SAML connection scoped to the pilot org.

[05:40] Aaron Li: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys in AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM? we require that encryption keys are customer-owned.
[05:50] Ravi Patel: yes, we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and external HSM integration for higher assurance. for Dedicated we can configure envelope encryption with customer keys and avoid key material ever touching Redwood-managed keys.

[06:05] Kelvin Ortiz: what about model data retention — do you store prompts/replies by default? and can we opt out?
[06:12] Maya Chen: by default we do not retain customer prompts/replies for any longer than necessary for service quality; for enterprise pilot we can disable storage, or set a short retention window. we also offer opt-out of using customer data to improve models.

[06:30] Lauren Gomez: audit trail needs to include user-level activity (who invoked which model, prompt hash, timestamp) and admin actions (role changes, key rotation).
[06:40] Ravi Patel: we log request metadata, auth principal, model version, and have an immutable audit chain exportable to S3 or pushed to your SIEM. we can include hashed prompt identifiers rather than plain text for privacy.

[07:02] Tom Rivera: legal/BAA — because we may have PHI in test data, do you sign BAAs?
[07:10] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood can enter a BAA for covered PHI use cases; that's part of enterprise contracting. for the pilot we can do data minimization and masked datasets to avoid PHI in the early benchmark.

[07:30] Lauren Gomez: timeline question again — if Redwood shares SOC2 and ISO docs by Monday, and we provision Dedicated pilot by Friday, can we run benchmarks the following week?
[07:40] Maya Chen: that's feasible. we'll send docs by Monday 6/14, propose to provision pilot environment by 6/19, and run bench week of 6/22.

[08:05] Aaron Li: regarding network restrictions — can we lock egress to specific subnets and restrict outbound calls?
[08:13] Ravi Patel: for Dedicated we can restrict egress and configure NAT rules; Private VPC gives even stronger controls. we also support IP allowlists for management plane access.

[08:32] Priya Shah: need to confirm separation of logs and ability to audit admin actions by vendor staff — we require privileged access reviews and break-glass workflows.
[08:42] Maya Chen: agreed; we provide RBAC, admin role scoping, and emergency access with documented approvals. we can also provide session recording/traces for admin sessions.

[09:00] Ravi Patel: on the performance side, we should agree on benchmark metrics: P50, P95, P99 latency (generation start to final token), tokens/sec throughput, average cost per 1k tokens, and quality metrics (your labeled accuracy). Also error rates and model degradation over long prompts.
[09:22] Lauren Gomez: P95 under 400ms is a hard requirement for interactive flows; for batch summarization we can tolerate higher latency but want predictable throughput.

[09:40] Tom Rivera: any known gotchas for pilot interplay with our Okta config? like SP-initiated only vs IdP-initiated?
[09:47] Maya Chen: we support both, but SP-initiated is what we usually set. just need metadata and the ACS URL from our end. we'll send the SAML docs.

[10:05] Aaron Li: can we run the bench harness inside our cloud account or do you run it from Redwood? we prefer run-in-customer-account for realistic network/leak tests.
[10:15] Ravi Patel: we can run load generators in your account and instrument with our tracing hooks; that gives you full control. for quick parity runs we can also run from Redwood and reproduce results.

[10:35] Priya Shah: encryption in transit — TLS 1.2+ okay? do you support mTLS for service-to-service?
[10:42] Maya Chen: TLS 1.2/1.3 supported; mTLS is available for private link connections and service endpoints on Dedicated.

[11:00] Lauren Gomez: another compliance question — do you have a pen test report or vulnerability management evidence?
[11:07] Maya Chen: yes, we have quarterly pen test reports and a vulnerability disclosure program; we'll include the attestation and summary redactions in the security pack.

[11:25] Ravi Patel: small architecture note — if we enable KV caching and prefix caching, you may see reduced latency for repeated prompts. for the pilot dataset we can configure caching to mimic production.

[11:43] Aaron Li: are there limitations on the models we can run in Dedicated? licensed models?
[11:48] Maya Chen: we surface a catalog; some licensed third-party models require additional contracts. generally open models and Redwood-verified variants are available. we'll list any license constraints in the pilot doc.

[12:05] Tom Rivera: what about rollback/fallback strategies if the model degrades? we'd like automated fallback to a lower-capacity model or queueing to keep latency SLOs.
[12:15] Ravi Patel: we support routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants; we can set canary rollouts to minimize impact. that's part of the rollout control.

[12:40] Priya Shah: audit logs detail again — do logs include full prompts? we prefer hashed pointers and allow storing encrypted blobs in our S3.
[12:50] Maya Chen: we can hash prompts in the logs and optionally push encrypted full request/response blobs to your S3 under your key. that meets your privacy requirements while allowing full forensics.

[13:10] Lauren Gomez: for the pilot success criteria let's state them explicitly: 1) P95 latency <400ms for interactive set, 2) model quality within 5% of our baseline on labeled dataset, 3) clear security check — SOC2/ISO artifacts reviewed and SSO + KMS configured, and 4) cost per 1k tokens within proposed estimate.

[13:35] Maya Chen: sounds good. we'll include these in the pilot scope doc and mark pass/fail thresholds.

[13:52] Aaron Li: performance isolation question — if other tenants spike, will Dedicated protect us?
[13:58] Ravi Patel: Dedicated is designed for capacity isolation. we also offer priority queueing and reserved slots to guarantee throughput; for total isolation Private is the option.

[14:20] Tom Rivera: integration with our CI/CD for model updates — do you have API hooks for model version pinning and rollout automation?
[14:28] Maya Chen: yes, model pinning and rollout APIs exist and we can integrate with your CI to trigger deployments, and Redwood Console provides canary controls.

[14:45] Priya Shah: legal — audit evidence: can we get exported logs and attestations for the pilot period?
[14:52] Maya Chen: yes, we'll provide exported logs, signed attestations, and a checklist for auditors.

[15:10] Ravi Patel: operationally for the bench we'll need sample payloads, auth tokens, SSO metadata if we test auth flows, and confirmation of dataset locations. Aaron, can you provide that?
[15:19] Aaron Li: yes we'll prepare sample payloads and a masked dataset for bench and provide Okta metadata.

[15:35] Lauren Gomez: what about cost estimate for a 2-week Dedicated pilot? we need a ballpark to get budget sign-off.
[15:42] Maya Chen: rough ballpark for the proposed 8-GPU pool for 2 weeks including support and logging add-ons would be $XXk— we'll send a detailed quote. (note: placeholder number - exact price to be sent in follow-up)

[16:05] Tom Rivera: are there any compliance blockers we should be aware of for the pilot?
[16:11] Kelvin Ortiz: from my side the main blockers are BAA for PHI, KMS customer key ownership, and immutable audits; if Redwood can provide those we're good to run the pilot.

[16:22] Maya Chen: we can support those. BAA will be part of contracting, KMS customer-owned keys on Dedicated, and immutable audit exports.

[16:40] Priya Shah: for SSO, do you support SCIM for user provisioning? we want to automate role assignment.
[16:47] Ravi Patel: yes, SCIM provisioning is supported for user sync and role mapping to our RBAC model.

[17:05] Lauren Gomez: for the pilot dataset we want to sample three workflows: triage chat, discharge summary summarization, and billing code extraction. we'll provide labeled sets for each.

[17:18] Ravi Patel: perfect, we'll map those to quality checks and automated evals.

[17:35] Aaron Li: tracing — do you provide request-level traces that can be correlated with our APM?
[17:41] Maya Chen: yes we emit trace IDs and can integrate with common tracing systems; we can also provide a read-only view in the console for the pilot.

[18:00] Tom Rivera: let's talk schedule, recap next steps and owners?
[18:05] Maya Chen: recap: Maya to send security pack (SOC2, ISO, pen test summary) and pilot scope doc by 6/14; Ravi to size GPU pool and bench harness and propose instance types by 6/16; Aaron to send sample datasets, Okta metadata, and peak QPS confirmation by 6/16; Priya to confirm legal/BAA needs by 6/18; Redwood to provision Dedicated pilot by 6/19 and run bench week of 6/22.

[18:30] Lauren Gomez: that timeline works for us if we get the docs Monday.

[18:35] Maya Chen: great. any final questions?
[18:40] Kelvin Ortiz: one last thing — vulnerability disclosure and change notification cadence. we need quarterly security updates and notifications for material changes.

[18:50] Maya Chen: we'll include cadence in the support SLA and include security contact info.

[19:05] Tom Rivera: okay thanks everyone, look forward to the doc.

[19:09] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with attachments and calendar invite for bench.

[54:20] (meeting ends)
